days.e: Mission 425: 1,548 bombers sent against 14 strategic targets in N Germany and V-weapon sites in the Pas de Calais; 49 bombers lost.
days.n: ~370 B-26s/A-20s bomb 9 V-weapon sites and the Houlgate coastal battery; 1,000+ fighters hit rail, bridges and troops over the front, Cherbourg peninsula and south to Dreux.

ground.u: First Army's VII Corps continues rapidly toward Cherbourg, 9th and 79th Divs coming up against a semicircular belt of fortifications 4-6 miles from the city. 9th Div's 60th Inf moves N through Vasteville to positions just short of Hill 170; 79th Div reaches positions between St Martin-le-Gréard and Bois de Roudou. In XIX Corps area, 29th Div makes a limited and futile effort to reduce the Villiers-Fossard salient.
ground.b: Gen Montgomery decides the British offensive cannot begin before 25 June since arrival of VIII Corps units has been delayed.

air.n: V-weapon sites in the Pas de Calais area

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.e: Mission 428: 1,234 bombers to Germany; first FRANTIC shuttle (UK to USSR) bombs the Ruhland synthetic oil plant; 45 bombers lost.
days.n: 250+ B-26s/A-20s bomb 13 V-weapon sites in the Pas de Calais; 700+ fighters escort and hit bridges S and W of Paris.

ground.u: First Army's VII Corps: while 9th and 79th Divs patrol and reorganize for the final assault on Cherbourg, 4th Div closes along the city's main defenses. 22d Inf gets a battalion on Hill 158, cutting the lateral road between Cherbourg and St Pierre-Eglise. At night Gen Collins issues an ultimatum to the garrison commander, Lt Gen Karl-Wilhelm von Schlieben, to surrender by 0900 on the 22d.

days.e: Mission 431 against targets in France; shuttle B-17s in the USSR moved east after the Poltava raid.
days.n: ~600 B-26s/A-20s and 1,200+ fighters pound the tip of the Cherbourg peninsula ahead of the US VII Corps assault on Cherbourg.

ground.u: VII Corps, receiving no reply to the ultimatum, begins the final assault on Cherbourg fortress. Intense air preparation from 1240 does more to demoralize the enemy than to damage his positions; the attack opens at 1400. 9th Div presses NE toward Cherbourg; 60th Inf takes Acqueville but is halted at the edge of the Flottemanville fortifications.

days.e: Mission 435: 212 heavies attack 12 CROSSBOW (V-weapon) sites; P-51s then strafe transport around Paris.
days.n: 175+ B-26s/A-20s bomb 7 V-weapon sites in the afternoon; ~630 fighters hit rail and road traffic.

ground.u: VII Corps penetrates the outer defenses of Cherbourg. 9th Div's 60th Inf overruns the Flottemanville area and 47th completes capture of Hill 171. 79th Div makes limited progress near La Mare à Canards. In 4th Div zone, 12th Inf, assisted by tanks, advances steadily toward Tourlaville.
ground.b: Unloading on the beaches resumes as the storm abates.

days.e: Mission 438: 967 bombers; B-17s hit Bremen oil targets and a Wesermünde aircraft factory.
days.n: 430+ B-26s/A-20s hit gun positions, V-sites, fuel dumps and rail targets; fighters range W of Paris and S of the Loire.

ground.u: VII Corps closes in on Cherbourg. 9th Div's 47th and 39th Regts move in on the city, toward Equeurdreville fort and Octeville. 79th Div's 314th Inf overruns La Mare à Canards and pushes toward Fort du Roule. 12th Inf continues the main effort of 4th Div.

air.n: V-weapon sites in the Pas de Calais area

days.e: Mission 441: 658 bombers to France: Toulouse airfields, Montbartier oil depot and many targets in N France.
days.n: 400+ B-26s/A-20s hit fuel dumps (Forêt d'Andaine, Écouves, Senonches) and rail bridges near Chartres.

ground.u: Naval gunfire supplements aerial and ground bombardment as the battle for Cherbourg nears its end. 9th Div's 47th Inf drives into the W suburbs, overrunning the fort at Equeurdreville and Redoute des Fourches. 79th Div's 314th Inf gains the upper defenses of Fort du Roule; 313th gets into the outskirts of Cherbourg.
ground.b: British Second Army opens its offensive west of Caen (Operation EPSOM begins 26 June).

days.e: FRANTIC B-17s bomb Drohobycz, Poland, from the USSR and fly on to Italy.
days.n: Weather cancels nearly all operations as US ground forces capture Cherbourg.

ground.u: 39th Inf drives through Octeville and Cherbourg to the coast, taking Gen von Schlieben, the fortress commander, and Rear Adm Hennecke prisoner; Schlieben refuses to surrender the entire fortress. 79th Div completes capture of Fort du Roule. 22d Inf, 4th Div, begins attack on Maupertus airfield.

days.e: Mission 443: 251 bombers hit V-weapon supply sites around Pas de Calais, Creil and Chantilly.
days.n: No bombers (weather); 700+ fighters cover the assault area and hit rail and road traffic.

ground.u: Organized resistance at Cherbourg ceases during the morning when the deputy fortress commander surrenders the arsenal to 47th Inf, 9th Div. 4th Div takes over garrisoning of Cherbourg; its 22d Inf overruns Maupertus airfield and clears Cap Lévy. Engineer units arrive to restore the port.

days.e: Mission 445: 992 bombers to France, Germany and Belgium; B-17s hit Laon, Juvincourt and Le Bourget airfields and Fismes bridge.
days.n: 220+ France-based fighters attack rail, bridges, dumps, artillery and troops.

ground.u: 79th Div, relieved in Cherbourg, moves S to the VIII Corps zone. 9th Div prepares to clear Cap de la Hague. In British Second Army area, 30 Corps secures Brettevillette but loses it to counterattack; 8 Corps expands its Odon bridgehead near Baron and secures another near Gavrus.

days.e: Mission 447: 1,150 bombers to Germany; B-17s hit Böhlen oil plant and Wittenberg.
days.n: ~200 B-26s/A-20s bomb Cap de la Hague batteries and rail lines around Rennes, St-Hilaire-du-Harcouët and Vitré.

ground.u: 9th Div attacks to clear Cap de la Hague and halts before the enemy line through Gruchy, Gréville and the crossroads SE of Beaumont-Hague. Forts in Cherbourg harbor surrender. 101st A/B Div starts from St Sauveur-le-Vicomte to Cherbourg.

days.e: Mission 448: 153 bombers hit Montdidier, Le Culot, Coxyde, Conches and Évreux airfields.
days.n: 125+ B-26s/A-20s blind-bomb fuel dumps and road junctions at Condé-sur-Vire, Conches and Thury-Harcourt.

ground.u: Montgomery orders First Army to make a breakout attack while British Second Army continues efforts to take Caen. The enemy line on Cap de la Hague collapses under 9th Div attacks. 101st A/B Div relieves 4th Div at Cherbourg, and the latter starts S for the coming offensive.

days.e: Mission 449: V-weapon mission recalled for cloud; 9 B-24s bomb Mont Louis Ferme.
days.n: IX Air Defense Command activated; weather stops bombers; fighters work the Vire area.

ground.u: First Army Field Order No. 1 prescribes a general offensive to open on 3 July by VIII Corps on the W flank, extended eastward by the other corps. Organized resistance on the Cherbourg peninsula ceases as 9th Div reaches the tip of Cap de la Hague. British Second Army repels counterattacks between Tilly-sur-Seulles and Caen.

air.n: V-weapon site at Mont Louis Ferme

days.e: Mission 450: 350 bombers hit 13 V-weapon sites in the Pas de Calais.
days.n: Bombers grounded; fighters cover Caen and the beaches and hit targets near La Haye-du-Puits.

ground.u: First Army regroups: VII Corps (4th, 9th, 83d Divs) is committed between VIII and XIX Corps. VIII Corps has 8th, 79th, 82d A/B and 90th Divs; XIX Corps 29th and 30th; V Corps 1st and 2d Inf and 2d Armd Divs. 3d Armd and 101st A/B Divs are in army reserve.

days.e: Shuttle B-17s in Italy join the Fifteenth AF against Arad, Romania.
days.n: ~275 fighters strafe and bomb strongpoints near Lessay and Périers ahead of First Army.

ground.u: First Army opens the general offensive that becomes the Battle of the Hedgerows. VIII Corps attacks south down the W coast of the Cotentin toward La Haye-du-Puits with 79th, 82d A/B and 90th Divs in driving rain that prevents air support; 82d A/B Div gains Hill 131.

days.e: Mission 451: 558 bombers sent against 7 airfields N and W of Paris (Dreux, Conches and others).
days.n: 95 B-26s/A-20s bomb Oissel bridge and positions N of Anneville-sur-Mer; 900+ fighters active.

ground.u: VIII Corps makes slow progress south; 82d A/B Div takes Hill 95 overlooking La Haye-du-Puits. VII Corps opens its attack on a narrow front between the Prairies Marécageuses and the Taute; 83d Div, in action for the first time, heads for Périers but makes negligible progress.

days.e: Mission 453: airfields in the Netherlands and Belgium (Gilze-Rijen, Volkel) and V-weapon supply sites in France.
days.n: ~180 B-26s/A-20s bomb bridges at Caen and four NOBALL headquarters.

ground.u: 35th Div begins landing on the Continent. VIII Corps overruns the railroad station of La Haye-du-Puits. VII Corps makes slow progress toward Périers.

days.e: Mission 455: 800 bombers hit 18 V-weapon sites in the Pas de Calais; second force to Germany.
days.n: ~500 B-26s/A-20s bomb bridges and rail lines at 8 places; 15+ fighter groups fly armed reconnaissance.

ground.u: Third Army establishes its HQ in France at Néhou. VIII Corps closes in on La Haye-du-Puits, which is nearly enveloped. VII Corps commits 4th Div W of 83d as the attack toward Périers continues against unabated opposition.

days.e: Mission 458: 1,129 bombers against oil plants (Leuna-area Lützkendorf, Halle) and aircraft plants (Bernburg, Aschersleben).
days.n: 100+ bombers hit a rail bridge near Tours and targets around Lisieux.

ground.u: 79th and 90th Divs continue to try to break through in the La Haye-du-Puits–Mont Castre Forest area. VII Corps inches down the Carentan-Périers road. XIX Corps crosses the Vire.
ground.b: RAF Bomber Command drops 2,662 tons on Caen during the night of 7-8 July ahead of the British assault.

days.e: Mission 460: 1,029 bombers sent against bridges, tunnels and V-sites in France; weather limits bombing.
days.n: ~280 bombers hit V-weapon HQ, strongpoints in the Caen battle area and bridges at Mantes, Saumur and Nantes.

ground.u: VIII Corps overruns La Haye-du-Puits; newly arrived 8th Div enters the line. VII Corps continues down the Carentan-Périers road. In XIX Corps area, 30th Div and 3d Armd Div expand the Vire bridgehead.
ground.b: British and Canadian troops attack Caen (Operation CHARNWOOD).

days.e: Mission 462: 150 B-17s hit bridges and Châteaudun airfield as targets of opportunity.
days.n: ~60 bombers hit bridges at Ablis, Orléans and Vendôme; fighters cover the battle area.

ground.u: VIII Corps makes little headway beyond La Haye-du-Puits. In VII Corps area, 4th and 83d Divs gain several hundred yards toward Périers; 83d overruns St Eny. 9th Div arrives from Cherbourg and takes a sector E of the Taute.
ground.b: British forces clear Caen north of the Orne.

days.e: Night leaflet and CARPETBAGGER sorties only.
days.n: Fighters bomb gun positions, bridges and troop concentrations over the battle area.

ground.u: VIII Corps advances about 3,000 yards beyond La Haye-du-Puits; 90th Div overruns Mont Castre Forest. VII Corps reaches the vicinity of St Eny, Tribehou and Le Désert. CCB, 3d Armd Div, is stopped just short of Hauts-Vents.
ground.b: Montgomery issues orders for the offensive, including the southward drive by First Army (COBRA).

days.e: Mission 466: 1,176 bombers to Germany; 371 B-17s hit the Munich marshalling yard.
days.n: Bombers strike fuel dumps at Forêt d'Andaine and Écouves; fighters attack around Lessay, Périers and St-Lô.

ground.u: First Army attacks with four corps abreast as V Corps joins in. VII Corps bears the brunt of a strong German counterattack (Panzer Lehr) on its left; enemy tanks penetrate 9th Div lines at Le Désert but positions are restored by infantry, tanks, TDs, artillery and aircraft.

days.e: Mission 469: 1,124 bombers bomb Munich.
days.n: 300+ bombers hit fuel dumps, Forêt de Cinglais concentrations and rail bridges (Saumur, Nantes, Nogent-le-Roi).

ground.u: 101st A/B Div returns to England. VIII Corps makes substantial progress toward the Ay and Sèves rivers; 8th Div overruns Hill 92. XIX Corps continues its attack on St Lô; 30th Div is held up near Pont Hébert.

days.e: Mission 471: 1,043 bombers to Germany; 356 B-17s bomb Munich again.
days.n: Weather stops bombers; fighters work the Sens-Montargis and Dreux-Évreux-Chartres areas.

ground.u: First Army approves the outline plan for COBRA, the breakout attack in the St Lô area. VIII Corps continues south; 9th Div nears Les Champs-de-Losque. XIX Corps continues the costly battle for St Lô.

days.e: Mission 472: 319 B-17s drop 3,700 supply containers to the French Resistance.
days.n: 62 bombers hit the Bourth embankment and Merey bridge; air battle near Brezolles and Alençon.

ground.u: VIII Corps closes along the Ay and Sèves rivers and halts by army order. 119th Inf, 30th Div, captures Pont Hébert. 35th Div breaks through to the Pont Hébert–St Lô highway; 29th Div holds NE and E of St Lô.

days.e: Mission 474: 169 P-38s/P-47s attack transport SE of Paris.
days.n: Weather cancels most operations; fighters hit targets around St-Lô, Argentan and Falaise.

ground.u: First Army halts its offensive W of the Taute to regroup for COBRA. VIII Corps holds its objectives along the Ay except Lessay. VII Corps continues with 9th Div while regrouping 30th and 1st Inf and 2d and 3d Armd Divs.

days.e: Mission 476: 1,087 bombers hit Munich, Augsburg and Stuttgart.
days.n: ~375 bombers hit strongpoints near St-Lô and bridges and a fuel dump SE of Rennes.

ground.u: VII Corps continues toward the Périers–St Lô road; 30th Div deepens its salient beyond Le Mesnil-Durand. 29th Div tries in vain to relieve the isolated 2d Bn, 116th Inf, astride the Bayeux–St Lô road.

days.e: Mission 478: 670 bombers hit tactical targets in France (Auxerre, Péronne, Anizy and more).
days.n: 69 B-26s hit Rennes fuel dumps; fighters dive-bomb defences at Coutances for First Army.

ground.u: 4th Armd Div is placed under VIII Corps. 9th Div breaks through the enemy main line on the corps right and drives toward the St Lô highway. In XIX Corps area, 35th Div penetrates enemy positions; 137th Inf reaches Rampan.

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.e: Mission 481: 644 B-24s join RAF Bomber Command in Operation GOODWOOD bombing E of Caen (Solier, Frénouville).
days.n: 400+ B-26s/A-20s support British Second Army around Caen.

ground.u: XIX Corps captures St Lô, concluding the Battle of the Hedgerows and giving First Army positions for the breakout (COBRA).
ground.b: British Second Army opens Operation GOODWOOD E of Caen after heavy bombing.

base: IX TAC advanced landing grounds, Normandy

days.e: Mission 482: 1,082 bombers hit W and SW Germany: chemical, aircraft and ball-bearing plants and marshalling yards.
days.n: 262 bombers hit Loire and Seine bridges and the Bruz fuel dump.

ground.u: XIX Corps mops up in St Lô; 35th Div takes over the whole corps sector, relieving 29th Div.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps takes Louvigny, Fleury and Ifs; 8 Corps: Cagny falls to the Guards Armd Div.

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.e: Mission 484: 1,172 bombers against oil and industry in central Germany (Dessau, Leipzig, Köthen).
days.n: 62 bombers hit the Senonches fuel dump and Chaulnes marshalling yard.

ground.u: First Army prepares for COBRA, shifting 4th Div from VIII to VII Corps. 134th Inf, 35th Div, relieves 29th Div's task force in St Lô.
ground.b: British: Bourguébus and Frénouville fall, ending GOODWOOD. In East Prussia the attempt to assassinate Hitler fails.

days.e: Mission 486: 1,110 bombers; B-24s hit Munich, Saarbrücken and Oberpfaffenhofen.
days.n: Weather stops all combat operations.

ground.u: Heavy rain stops operations along the front; First Army continues to prepare for COBRA.

days.e: Leaflet sorties over Bremen, Hamburg and Kiel; night CARPETBAGGER flights.
days.n: Bombers hit Bourth bridge and fuel dumps at Forêt de Conches and Flers.

ground.u: In VIII Corps area, 90th Div elements reach St Germain-sur-Sèves but are forced to withdraw.
ground.b: British 43d Div takes Maltot.

days.e: Mission 490: 280 bombers hit Creil, Laon and Juvincourt airfields.
days.n: 330+ bombers hit bridges on the Argentan-Paris and Lisieux-Évreux railways.

ground.u: First Army waits for weather suitable for the COBRA air bombardment.
ground.b: Canadian First Army (Gen Crerar) takes control of British 1 Corps on the E flank.

days.e: Mission 492: 1,586 bombers sent for Operation COBRA W of St-Lô; attack postponed for weather.
days.n: COBRA groups recalled; B-26s hit rail bridges and dumps.

ground.u: Air preparation for COBRA begins, but weather is so poor that the ground attack is postponed; some bombs fall short on US troops.

days.e: Mission 494: 1,581 bombers saturation-bomb the Marigny-St-Gilles area W of St-Lô to open COBRA.
days.n: 11 B-26/A-20 groups bomb near St-Lô; afternoon attacks on Seine and Loire bridges.

ground.u: First Army launches the COBRA breakout in VII Corps zone. Saturation bombing by the Eighth and Ninth Air Forces, more than 4,000 tons in a small area, stuns the enemy; some bombs fall short, causing US casualties. Lt Gen McNair is killed by a bomb while watching the attack.

days.e: Mission 496: P-47s hit St-Just marshalling yards and the Givet fuel dump.
days.n: ~160 bombers hit the Senonches fuel dump; fighters give close support around St-Lô.

ground.u: VIII Corps joins COBRA, attacking with 8th, 90th and 83d Divs; 8th Div cuts the Lessay-Périers road. VII Corps commits more units; 1st Div seizes Marigny and CCB, 3d Armd Div, drives SW of it.

days.e: Mission 498: B-24s hit Brussels/Vilvoorde, Gravelines and Ghent.
days.n: Fighters hit targets around Coutances and St-Lô as US forces break through west of St-Lô.

ground.u: VIII Corps is held up more by obstacles than by opposition; 79th Div overruns Lessay and 90th occupies Périers. 6th Armd Div is committed through 8th Div.

air.n: Oil installations and industrial plants Ghent

days.e: Mission 501: 1,057 bombers to Belgium, France and Germany (incl. Merseburg area).
days.n: IX Bomber Command hits bridges and dumps around Conches, Dreux and Le Mans for First Army.

ground.u: First Army orders exploitation and rapid pursuit. VIII Corps commits 6th and 4th Armd Divs; CCB, 4th Armd Div, takes Coutances by 1700. With the fall of Coutances, COBRA has largely accomplished its purpose.

days.e: Mission 503: 569 B-17s hit the Merseburg/Leuna synthetic oil plant.
days.n: Bombers grounded; fighters range over Rouen, Amiens, Tours, Vendôme and Le Mans.

ground.u: VIII Corps pursues with 6th and 4th Armd Divs abreast; CCA, 4th Armd Div, reaches Cérences. Enemy columns retreating from Roncey toward St Denis-le-Gast suffer very heavy losses under air, artillery and tank attack.

days.e: Administrative day (VIII Air Force Composite Command order).
days.n: 450+ bombers hit defences around Chaumont in support of First Army.

ground.u: 6th and 4th Armd Divs speed toward Granville and Avranches; CCB, 4th Armd Div, pushes into Avranches and captures bridges over the Sée.
ground.b: British Second Army opens Operation BLUECOAT south of Caumont.

days.e: Mission 507: 567 B-17s bomb Munich; others hit Munich-Allach and Schleissheim.
days.n: ~500 bombers attack bridges on the Seine, Loire and Mayenne.

ground.u: 6th Armd Div's CCR overruns Granville. 4th Armd Div probes south from Avranches and secures a crossing of the Sélune near Pontaubault, opening the way into Brittany.

days.e: Mission 508: 1,291 bombers; supply drops to the Resistance in SE France plus airfields and bridges.
days.n: XIX Tactical Air Command becomes operational with Third Army; B-26s hit Seine bridges.

ground.u: 12th Army Group (Gen Bradley) becomes operational, commanding US First and Third Armies; Montgomery retains command of all ground forces through August. XIX TAC begins supporting Third Army.
ground.b: British 11th Armd Div overruns Le Bény-Bocage.

days.n: Bombing in Brittany halted unless 12th Army Group asks; Seine bridges attacked.

ground.u: Bradley orders Third Army to secure St Hilaire-du-Harcouët–Fougères–Rennes and clear Brittany, bypassing St Malo if necessary. 6th Armd Div bypasses Dinan. 79th Div moves to XV Corps for the drive on Fougères.

days.n: 180+ bombers hit rail targets at Mantes, Chartres and Maintenon.

ground.u: Third Army is to clear Brittany with minimum forces and secure the Mayenne crossings; First Army extends toward Mayenne-Domfront. 6th Armd Div nears Loudéac before being ordered back toward Dinan.

air.n: V-weapon sites in the Pas de Calais

days.e: Mission 514: 1,307 bombers; B-17s hit Hamburg and Bremen oil refineries.
days.n: 62 bombers hit bridges at Oissel and Épernon; fighters hit dumps at Angers and Tours.

ground.u: The attack on Dinan is cancelled and 6th Armd Div heads for Brest, reaching Carhaix. Rennes falls to 13th Inf, 8th Div. 4th Armd Div drives toward Vannes.
ground.b: Montgomery orders Canadian First Army to attack toward Falaise as soon as possible.

days.e: Mission 519: 1,171 bombers hit Magdeburg-Brunswick-Hannover oil, tank and aircraft plants.
days.n: Ninth AF HQ moves to St-Sauveur-Lendelin beside 12th Army Group.

ground.u: VIII Corps attacks W, SW, S and E at once. 6th Armd Div bypasses Carhaix toward Brest; 83d Div attacks the outer defenses of St Malo. Brittany is cut off as CCA, 4th Armd Div, reaches Vannes. XV Corps: 90th Div seizes Mayenne; 79th nears Laval.

days.e: Mission 524: 1,186 bombers; Brandenburg and Genshagen plants, V-sites in France.
days.n: Bombers hit Beauvais, Blois and Forêt de Perseigne; fighters cover Vire, Rennes and Redon.

ground.u: 12th Army Group orders a bridgehead over the Sarthe at Le Mans–Alençon. 6th Armd Div overcomes opposition near Morlaix; 83d Div hammers at St Malo. Germans counterattack toward Mortain (night 6-7).

days.e: Mission 527: 905 bombers sent against fuel dumps and bridges in France; heavy cloud.
days.n: IX and XIX TAC form mobile HQs to follow First and Third Armies east.

ground.u: 6th Armd Div closes in on Brest, too late to assault before the defenses are strengthened. 83d Div continues the battle for St Malo; 4th Armd Div invests Lorient. Around Mortain, First Army holds against the German counteroffensive.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps attacks S toward Falaise (TOTALIZE) after heavy bomber preparation.

days.e: Mission 530: 414 B-24s against airfields and V-sites; also Operation TOTALIZE support S of Caen.
days.n: Vandenberg takes command; 406 bombers hit bridges, Argentan-Alençon radar and targets near St-Malo.

ground.u: The surrender ultimatum to Brest is ignored. Bitter fighting continues in the outskirts of St Malo; 121st Inf meets strong opposition advancing on Dinard. XV Corps takes Le Mans.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps continues TOTALIZE astride the Caen-Falaise road.

days.e: Mission 533: 824 bombers to SE Germany; weather forces targets of opportunity.
days.n: ~400 bombers hit the Forêt de Blois dump, shipping at Brest and 10 rail bridges.

ground.u: 6th Armd Div leaves a force to contain Brest and moves N to meet a threat to its rear, virtually destroying an enemy division near Plouvien.
ground.b: Canadian 4th Armd Div overruns Bretteville-le-Rabet; Polish 1st Armd Div seizes Cauvicourt and St Sylvain.

days.e: Mission 537: 175 B-24s hit fuel dumps and bridges SE of Paris (Clamecy, Joigny, Sens).
days.n: ~200 bombers hit rail bridges around Paris; fighters reach Dijon and Troyes.

ground.u: VIII Corps attacks Dinard and the St Malo Citadel and contains Brest and Lorient; 4th Armd Div forces the enemy back into Nantes. XV Corps armor drives north toward Alençon and Sées. XX Corps: 5th Div overruns Angers.

days.e: Mission 541: 660 bombers hit marshalling yards, dumps and airfields in NE France and around Paris.
days.n: Bombers hit bridges at Oissel, Fismes and Creil and gun defences at St-Malo.

ground.u: The gap between Third Army forces moving north and Canadian and British forces moving south is about 20 miles. XV Corps: 2d French and 5th Armd Divs continue steadily northward against increasing rear-guard opposition.

days.e: FRANTIC shuttle ends with Toulouse/Francazal bombed en route to the UK.
days.n: Bombers hit roads around Argentan to bottle up German troops.

ground.u: 83d Div inches forward against the St Malo Citadel and Dinard. XV Corps reaches the Alençon area and drives toward Argentan.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps is held up on the road to Falaise.

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.e: Mission 548: 1,264 bombers hit coastal batteries and choke points between Le Havre and Paris.
days.n: ~575 bombers hit roads around Lisieux and to Rugles to contain the Falaise pocket.

ground.u: XV Corps reaches the Argentan area and is halted there by order of Gen Bradley. 83d Div continues slowly against St Malo and Dinard; 4th Armd Div finds Nantes free of the enemy; 8th Div advances to Dinan.

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England
IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England
IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.e: Mission 552: 1,183 bombers hit airfields and factories in SW Germany and E France.
days.n: Bridges and junctions beyond the line are hit; fighters work Falaise, Broglie and Chartres.

ground.u: V Corps of First Army pushes toward Tinchebray from the W; British 30 Corps closes on Vassy and Condé; 59th Div takes Thury-Harcourt. Third Army turns part of its force east toward Dreux, Chartres and Orléans.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps attacks to outflank opposition on the Caen-Falaise highway (TRACTABLE); RAF Bomber Command drops 3,723 tons in support.

days.e: Mission 554: 932 bombers hit 11 airfields in NW Germany, Netherlands and Belgium with the RAF.
days.n: Troop carriers fly the invasion of S France; 330+ bombers hit dumps near Beauvais and Chantilly.

ground.u: 83d Div takes Dinard; the enemy still holds the St Malo Citadel. XV Corps' 5th Armd and 79th Divs push rapidly toward Dreux. Allied forces land in southern France (DRAGOON).
ground.b: British 8 Corps meets US V Corps near Tinchebray.

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.e: Mission 556: 1,090 bombers hit oil and aircraft plants in central Germany (Delitzsch, Schkeuditz).
days.n: ~130 bombers hit Risle river bridges (Pont-Audemer, Brionne).

ground.u: 83d Div continues to batter the St Malo Citadel. Third Army forces take Dreux, Chartres and Orléans areas.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps has virtually surrounded Falaise; British 1 Corps begins advancing east toward the Seine.

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England
IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England
IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.e: Small Azon and BATTY guided-bomb trials; leaflets.
days.n: 400+ bombers hit Risle bridges; fighters cover St-Malo and Dreux.

ground.u: Bradley directs First Army to clear the Chambois-Trun area and, with the British, close the pocket; Third Army is to drive on Mantes-Gassicourt. The St Malo Citadel surrenders to 83d Div.
ground.b: British Second Army presses south against the pocket from Flers, Condé and Falaise.

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England
IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England
IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England
IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England
IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.e: Mission 561: B-24s hit Roye/Amy airfield and other targets.
days.n: 1,000+ fighters cover ground forces from Argentan to Paris and along the Seine.

ground.u: 2d Div moves to Brest to relieve 6th Armd Div. XV Corps' 5th Armd and 79th Divs drive toward the Seine at Mantes-Gassicourt. XX Corps: 7th Armd Div takes over the Dreux bridgehead; 5th Div moves to Chartres. 35th Div finishes mopping up Orléans.

days.n: No IX Bomber Command operations; fighters fly armed reconnaissance along the Seine.

ground.u: 79th Div enters Mantes-Gassicourt; 5th Armd Div starts north along the Seine toward Louviers. In First Army's V Corps area, 90th Div reaches Chambois and at 1930 contacts a Polish patrol, closing the Falaise-Argentan gap.
ground.b: British 11th Armd Div reaches the Argentan area.

days.n: 61 B-26s bomb German troops at Forêt de la Londe waiting to cross the Seine.

ground.u: 79th Div crosses the Seine at Mantes; 12th Army Group drives north across the British front toward the lower Seine to cut off the German retreat.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps frustrates the final German attempt to escape from the Falaise-Argentan pocket.

base: IX Bomber Command bases, Essex & S England

days.n: Weather grounds all bombers and fighters.

ground.u: First Army's V Corps is relieved near Argentan by British 30 Corps; 102d Cav Gp reconnoitres NE of Sées. Third Army forces push east beyond the Seine at Melun and toward Sens.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps drives east toward the Seine at Rouen.

days.n: Bombers grounded; fighters cover two infantry and one armoured division and sweep Évreux to Troyes.

ground.u: V Corps, now out of contact with the enemy, is given the mission of freeing Paris; the French 2d Armd Div is alerted. 4th Div joins V Corps.
ground.b: Deauville falls to the Belgian Brigade.

days.e: 142 P-47s hit rail transport from St-Omer to Reims.
days.n: Fighters cover ground forces and the Seine crossings.

ground.u: XIX Corps moves across the British front toward Elbeuf; V Corps' French 2d Armd and US 4th Divs move toward Paris.
ground.b: British 1 Corps makes slow progress in the coastal sector; 2 Corps is heavily engaged near Orbec.

days.e: Mission 568: 1,319 bombers hit aviation and oil targets in Germany (Brunswick area).
days.n: Bomber mission cancelled; fighters bomb Seine bridges and patrol Troyes, Orléans and Tours.

ground.u: XIX Corps nears Elbeuf and shells the Seine crossing sites. French 2d Armd Div and 4th Div close on Paris.
ground.b: Canadian 2d Div seizes Bernay and crosses the Risle at Nassandres; contact made with XIX Corps near Elbeuf.

days.e: Mission 570: 1,191 bombers hit aircraft plants, test stations and synthetic oil.
days.n: ~240 bombers attack strongpoints around Brest; Paris is liberated.

ground.u: XIX Corps overruns Elbeuf. In V Corps area, the French 2d Armd Div enters Paris from the SW at 0700 and 4th Div from the S; FFI and civilians help clear scattered strongpoints. The German commander of Paris surrenders.
ground.b: British 15th Div prepares to cross the Seine at Louviers.

days.e: Mission 575: 359 B-17s bomb gun batteries around Brest.
days.n: IX Bomber Command strikes fuel dumps north of the Seine.

ground.u: First Army is to support the British drive on the axis Paris-Brussels. XIX Corps is relieved by British forces; XV Corps holds the Mantes bridgehead. General de Gaulle leads a parade down the Champs-Élysées.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps prepares to cross the Seine south of Rouen; British 30 Corps expands its bridgehead at Vernon.

days.e: Missions 583+: Berlin raid recalled for cloud; scattered targets in N Germany.
days.n: Bombers hit troops around Rouen and fuel dumps near Laon.

ground.u: First Army begins to advance NE from the Paris area and the Mantes bridgehead.
ground.b: Canadian divisions cross the Seine between Elbeuf and Pont de l'Arche; British 15th Div crosses E of Louviers.

days.e: Weather stops heavies; 835 fighters strafe rail targets across the Low Countries, France and Germany.
days.n: Bombers hit dumps at Doullens and Compiègne.

ground.u: XV Corps improves the Mantes-Gassicourt bridgehead; 2d Armd Div joins to spearhead the breakout. Third Army crosses the Marne at Château-Thierry and approaches Reims.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps expands its bridgehead toward Rouen.

days.e: 104 fighters attack transport in France, Belgium and Germany.
days.n: Weather limits operations to one fuel dump and a few sweeps.

ground.u: Gasoline is acutely short and Third Army is given priority on air supply. XIX Corps takes over the XV Corps zone; 2d Armd Div drives to Magny-en-Vexin.
ground.b: British 15th Div holds a loop of the Seine W of Les Andelys.

days.e: Mission 590: 215 heavies hit 8 V-sites in the Pas de Calais; later U-boat pens.
days.n: ~75 bombers hit dumps near Arques-la-Bataille and guns on Île de Cézembre.

ground.u: XIX Corps drives rapidly NE; 2d Armd Div is within 10 miles of Beauvais. V Corps pursues NE toward Compiègne. VII Corps seizes Laon. Third Army crosses the Meuse.
ground.b: British 1 Corps begins crossing the Seine.

air.n: U-boat base and shipyards at Kiel

days.e: Night leaflet and CARPETBAGGER sorties.
days.n: 99 bombers hit Forêt d'Arques and Cézembre; fighters cover Amiens, St-Quentin and Arras.

ground.u: First Army drives toward the Belgian frontier; Third Army's advance stalls for lack of gasoline near the Meuse.
ground.b: Canadian 2 Corps attacks east from its Seine bridgehead toward Dieppe; British 7th Armd Div reaches the Poix-Aumale line; 11th Armd Div captures Amiens.

days.n: Brussels liberated and Antwerp largely cleared; fighters reconnoitre Belgium, Luxembourg and Germany.

ground.u: Eisenhower directs First Army toward the Ruhr and Third Army toward the Saar. Hitler reinstates Rundstedt as Commander in Chief West. British troops have entered Brussels (3 Sep) and Antwerp (4 Sep).
ground.b: Polish 1st Armd Div continues NE toward St Omer; Canadian 3d Div advances along the Pas de Calais coast.

days.e: Mission 681: 1,338 bombers PFF-attack Cologne marshalling yards (Eifeltor, Gremberg, Kalk).
days.n: All Rhine bridges cleared for attack; B-26s hit the Euskirchen rail bridge.

ground.u: First Army's VII Corps continues to tighten the ring around Aachen; 1st Div and 30th Div have closed the encirclement.
ground.b: British 3d Div takes Venray.
ground.s: US Seventh Army: 44th Div closes in the Lunéville area.

days.e: Mission 682: 300 B-17s PFF-bomb Kassel.
days.n: Weather; IX TAC covers the US 1st Infantry Division at Aachen.

ground.u: 12th Army Group plans: First Army is to cross the Rhine near Cologne between 1 and 5 November; Ninth Army covers its north flank; Third Army covers the right flank. Maj Gen McLain succeeds Gen Corlett at XIX Corps.
ground.s: US Seventh Army: 36th Div breaks into Bruyères.

days.e: Night leaflet sorties only.
days.n: Weather prevents all flying.

ground.u: The front is generally quiet as preparations for the November offensive continue. Eisenhower orders 6th Army Group to protect the south flank of 12th Army Group in the coming drive to the Rhine.
ground.b: US 104th Div moves into line along the Antwerp-Breda highway.
ground.s: US Seventh Army: 3d Div meets stronger resistance approaching Les Rouges Eaux on the road to St Dié.

days.e: 415 P-47s/P-51s attack airfields and ground targets in Germany.
days.n: Only fighter patrols over W Germany hitting rail targets.

ground.u: The front remains generally static.
ground.b: Canadians continue reducing the Breskens pocket and drive along the Beveland isthmus.
ground.s: French 1st Army plans its Belfort offensive (INDEPENDENCE).

days.e: Mission 688: 1,250 bombers hit oil and industry; Hamburg refineries (Harburg, Rhenania).
days.n: First Tactical Air Force (Prov) established; 9th Bomb Div grounded.

ground.u: First Army shifts the V/VII Corps boundary to give V Corps responsibility for Schmidt; 28th Div begins relieving 9th Div for the drive on Schmidt in the Hürtgen Forest.
ground.b: Canadian 2d Div reaches Rilland on the Beveland isthmus.
ground.s: US 44th Div holds against counterattacks E of the Forêt de Parroy.

days.e: Mission 689: 1,225 bombers hit Bielefeld, Münster and Hannover-area targets.
days.n: Fighters sweep from Metz to Cologne attacking rail and road traffic.

ground.u: 102d Div enters combat with Ninth Army's XIX Corps. 28th Div takes over the 9th Div zone; 9th Div goes back to Camp Elsenborn.
ground.b: British 52d Div lands on South Beveland from Terneuzen.
ground.s: US 3d Div pushes toward St Dié.

air.n: Welheim synthetic oil plant at Bottrop

days.e: Night leaflet sorties.
days.n: Fighters patrol E France and W Germany and support Seventh Army near Metz.

ground.u: The 12th Army Group front stays quiet while supply builds up; 28th Div prepares to attack Schmidt on 2 November.
ground.b: Canadian 2d Div starts across the Walcheren causeway but is halted.
ground.s: French 2d Armd Div drives SE from the Forêt de Mondon.

days.e: Mission 935: 1,252 bombers hit jet airfields, oil storage and the Wolfratshausen munitions plant.
days.n: Ninth AF supports the advance across central Germany.

ground.u: Ninth Army's XIII Corps: 84th Div prepares to assault Hannover; CCR, 5th Armd Div, crosses the Leine S of Hannover and races toward the Oker. First Army reduces the Ruhr pocket from the south.
ground.b: British 30 Corps advances E and NE of Lingen.
ground.s: US Seventh Army: 45th and 3d Divs take the Hohe Rhön and prepare to drive on Nuremberg.

base: 9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium
9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium
9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium

days.e: Mission 941: 1,303 bombers hit the Freiham oil depot, Kraiburg munitions and other targets.
days.n: 689 medium bombers strike Bernburg, Oschersleben, Zwickau, Köthen and the Naumburg depot.

ground.u: Ninth Army: CCB, 2d Armd Div, in a record drive of 57 miles, reaches the Elbe S of Magdeburg. 5th Armd Div reaches the Altmark; 84th Div heads for the Elbe. Third Army's 4th Armd Div and First Army forces reach Weimar and the Saale; Buchenwald is liberated.
ground.b: Canadian 1st Div attacks across the IJssel toward Apeldoorn.
ground.s: XV Corps opens its drive SE toward Nuremberg.

base: 9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium

9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium

days.e: Mission 948: 1,167 bombers attack German pockets on the Gironde estuary.
days.n: Fighters support 3d Armored at the Elbe/Mulde junction near Dessau.

ground.u: Ninth Army: forward elements of 84th and 102d Divs reach the Elbe; evidence of mass Nazi atrocities is found at Gardelegen. First Army splits the Ruhr pocket.
ground.b: Canadian 1 Corps clears Arnhem.
ground.s: XV Corps clears Bamberg and pushes toward Nuremberg.

days.e: Night leaflets; CARPETBAGGER to Norway.
days.n: XIX TAC covers the Third Army front around Bayreuth and Nürnberg.

ground.u: Ninth Army's XIII Corps (29th Inf, 5th Armd Divs) continues to the Elbe; Lüchow surrenders. 84th Div clears its sector along the Elbe NW of Wittenberge.
ground.s: 12th Armd Div reaches the Danube at Dillingen and seizes a bridge.

days.e: Night leaflets; First TAF HQ 71st Fighter Wing moves to Heidelberg.
days.n: Weather cancels most Ninth AF operations.

ground.u: 5th Armd Div finishes clearing its Elbe sector; Dannenberg surrenders. 75th Div begins relieving 5th Div south of the Ruhr. First Army releases 4th Armd Div to Third Army.
ground.b: British 12 Corps enters Harburg, opposite Hamburg.
ground.s: XV Corps takes 20th Armd Div to spearhead the drive on Munich.

days.e: Night leaflet sorties.
days.n: Weather limits operations.

ground.u: 29th Div relieves 5th Armd Div along the Elbe; 84th Div waits on the river for Soviet forces. First Army: 9th Div takes over the Mulde line; Wurzen surrenders to 69th Div.
ground.b: British 30 Corps prepares to assault Bremen.
ground.s: 45th and 42d Divs drive south toward the Danube.

days.e: Mission 968: the Eighth's final heavy-bomber raid on an industrial target: Pilsen Skoda works and rail targets.
days.n: 296 bombers hit Erding airfield and Freilassing; fighters support XII Corps on the Danube.

ground.u: XIII Corps ends offensive operations except patrolling across the Elbe and begins occupation duties. In First Army's V Corps area, 69th Div patrols meet Soviet forces at Torgau and Strehla on the Elbe, the first link-up of US and Soviet armies.
ground.b: British 30 Corps enters Bremen.
ground.s: 45th and 42d Divs reach the Danube; 42d clears Donauwörth.

base: 9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium
9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium

days.e: Night leaflet and CARPETBAGGER sorties.
days.n: 125 bombers hit Plattling airfield; XII Corps crosses into Austria SE of Passau.

ground.u: Ninth Army: 102d Div relieves 35th Div along the Elbe. Third Army's XII Corps crosses into Austria SE of Passau.
ground.b: British 30 Corps completes capture of Bremen.
ground.s: 45th and 42d Divs cross the Danube.

base: 9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium

days.e: No combat missions.
days.n: Fighters cover XII Corps as 11th Armored reaches the Czech border toward Linz.

ground.u: Ninth and First Armies hold and adjust defensive positions. In Third Army's XII Corps area, 11th Armd Div patrols reach the Czech border N of Bischofsreuth; 26th Div clears Deggendorf.
ground.b: US XVIII Corps (A/B) concentrates at Uelzen under British Second Army.

days.n: Weather prevents all Ninth AF combat operations.

ground.u: First Army regroups along the Mulde; V Corps begins moving south toward Czechoslovakia.
ground.b: British 8 Corps prepares to cross the Elbe at Lauenburg.
ground.s: 20th Armd Div opens the drive on Munich.

days.e: Leaflets; First TAF HQ 64th Fighter Wing moves to Schwäbisch Hall.
days.n: Weather; fighters fly patrols.

ground.u: XIX Corps cavalry crosses the Elbe to Zerbst to seek the Red Army. First Army's VII Corps holds the Mulde; V Corps starts south to its new zone.
ground.b: British 8 Corps crosses the Elbe at Lauenburg.
ground.s: XV Corps races to the outskirts of Munich and overruns Dachau concentration camp.

days.e: Leaflet sorties.
days.n: XIX TAC supports XII Corps moving SE along the Danube.

ground.u: A troop of 125th Cav Sq meets the Soviet 121st Div at Apollensdorf. First Army's commander meets the Soviet 5th Guards Army commander at Eilenburg on the Mulde. Hitler commits suicide in Berlin.
ground.b: British 8 Corps expands its Elbe bridgehead.
ground.s: XV Corps clears Munich and takes the Isar bridges intact.

days.e: Mission 973 (CHOWHOUND): 396 B-17s drop food at The Hague and Rotterdam.
days.n: A-26s bomb Stod, Czechoslovakia; fighters dive-bomb Berchtesgaden.

ground.u: Ninth Army, its offensive over, holds the Elbe; mass surrenders of German troops continue. XVI Corps governs Westphalia and Lippe.
ground.b: British 11th Armd and 5th Divs pass through the Elbe bridgehead.
ground.s: XV Corps mops up around Munich.

base: 9th Bomb Division airfields, N France & Belgium

days.e: Mission 975: 401 B-17s drop food at Schiphol, Utrecht, Hilversum and Alkmaar.
days.n: Fighters patrol the Third Army front in Austria and Czechoslovakia.

ground.u: XIII Corps makes first contact with the Red Army near Balow. First Army's V Corps improves positions on the Czech frontier. Berlin surrenders to the Soviets.
ground.b: British Second Army reaches the Baltic, sealing off Schleswig-Holstein and Denmark.
ground.s: 3d Div prepares to drive on Salzburg.

days.e: Mission 977: 399 B-17s drop food in the Netherlands.

ground.u: First Army's V Corps relieves 97th and 90th Divs. Third Army's 11th Armd Div continues SE toward Linz, its final objective.
ground.b: Montgomery refuses the German offer to surrender all northern forces, including those facing the Red Army.
ground.s: 3d Div speeds toward Salzburg.

days.e: Night leaflet sorties.
days.n: XIX TAC supports XII Corps at Linz and XX Corps across the Inn.

ground.u: First Army HQ prepares to return to the US for redeployment to the Pacific. V Corps passes to Third Army for the final drive on Karlsbad and Pilsen.
ground.b: Germans sign the surrender of forces in Holland, NW Germany and Denmark at 1820, effective 0800 on 5 May.
ground.s: 7th Inf, 3d Div, reaches Berchtesgaden.

days.e: Mission 980: 403 B-17s drop food at Schiphol, Utrecht, Alkmaar and Hilversum.

ground.u: Ninth Army: 83d Div withdraws its Elbe bridgehead; 30th Div meets the Red Army on the Elbe. Third Army's V Corps attacks toward Pilsen with 97th Div and prepares for the drive on Karlsbad.
ground.b: 21 Army Group halts offensive operations at 0800 when the ceasefire takes effect.
ground.s: Army Group G accepts surrender terms at Haar, Bavaria; hostilities cease on the 6th Army Group front.
